This report runs under the attenuated check (#47, docs/DEBT.md row 36): the software workload declares glossary-lint's commit-message half advisory and its comment half blocking. So under the treatment arm the four units whose only drift was the word in the commit message — d1 to d4 — close on their first attempt, where the first sloppy report had them refused three times each for that word alone; each of those four commit messages lands on main and is recorded as an audit finding at advisory, which is why the treatment's vocabulary drift is four, not zero. The two units whose comments drift, d5 and d6, are still refused three times each by the comment half, so the README rule never lands (memoryRules 0 against the control's one) and neither do their comments. The lifts say it plainly: the treatment closes five of seven (−0.29), spends 1.71 attempts per unit against 1.14, and holds vocabulary drift to 3.43 against 5.86, an interval that overlaps the control's — one repetition of a scripted unit is an observation, not a distribution. The cost that was being paid is now visible as a choice: the strict check bought zero drift on main by refusing correct work; the attenuated one lets a word in a commit message through, on the record, and refuses only the drift that reaches the code. Which to pay is a workload's declaration — personal-finance keeps both halves blocking — and the arm without the check (no-glossary-lint) is the control's numbers again, so the check is doing exactly and only what its comment half says. What the memory tool did not change either: the sloppy unit had `remember` available and wrote the rule into the README anyway — the tool changes what a unit can do, not what a prose-preferring unit will do — and the rendered identity section that might is what a scripted run cannot see.

Under the treatment d5 and d6 were refused, so d7 branches from a base without d5's fix to test/dated.test.js, and it still closes, because d5's fix does not reach the archive tests either way.
